inferenceReason.title: Why is "{{column}}" typed this way?
inferenceReason.canChangeHint: If this is wrong, change the type using the selector on the left.

rule.boolean: Boolean columns are always treated as Categorical.
rule.dateExcluded: Date/time types are excluded from categorical detection.
rule.dateMappedToText: Values were detected as dates ({{baseType}} format), but dashAI does not yet have a Date type — the column is stored as Text and not classified as categorical.
rule.stringLooksLikeDate: Values look like dates, so the column was kept as text/date instead of categorical.
rule.tooManyUnique: Too many distinct values to be categorical (above the unique-count threshold).
rule.uniqueRatioAbove: Unique values represent too large a fraction of the rows — treated as numeric/text instead of categorical.
rule.stringTooLong: Average text length is too long to be a category label.
rule.stringHighVariance: Text length varies too much across values for a categorical interpretation.
rule.integerAllUnique: Every integer value is unique — looks like an identifier, not a category.
rule.integerSequentialRange: Integers form a sequential range (e.g. 1, 2, 3, ...) — treated as numeric, not categorical.
rule.integerDenseSmallRange: Integers form a dense small range — treated as numeric.
rule.floatHasDecimals: Float values have real decimals — treated as numeric, never categorical.
rule.lowCardinality: Few distinct values relative to row count — classified as Categorical.
rule.mlClassifierCategorical: The categorical classifier model scored this column above the categorical threshold.
rule.mlClassifierNotCategorical: The categorical classifier model did not consider this column categorical.
rule.emptyColumn: Column is empty — no inference performed.
rule.unsupportedBaseType: Base type is not eligible for categorical detection.
rule.unknown: No specific rule recorded for this classification.
